recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-7504 unless Patient Care separately revisits the broader Condition/Observation boundary for questionnaire-style medical-history or absence statements.
issue_request: FHIR-7504 was a Published Patient Care change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification, asking how "history of" should be captured and directing that a usage note on Condition.code say the code may include concepts such as "history of X" and "good health" when useful or appropriate.
initial_application: Git commit b8fddd3c06 (#7504, #7618, #8360 - added usage notes) added the requested sentence to source/condition/condition-notes.xml. After later source rework/deletion, commit 005f3df50a restored condition-notes with the same FHIR-7504 guidance still present.
additional_context: Condition is active in source/fhir.ini, making source/condition/condition-notes.xml part of the current resource build scope. Later Condition-code decisions added nearby no-known-problems and absence guidance (FHIR-8749, FHIR-11077) and FHIR-41624 left latent/history-like concerns to code/text instead of changing clinicalStatus. Zulip discussions quote and interpret the current guidance but do not show a later reversal.
reconciliation: No source edit was made. The current Condition notes already state that Condition.code may include "history of X" and "good health" when useful or appropriate, and duplicating the note in another location would not materially improve implementer understanding.

related_jiras.note: Applied in the same 2015 Condition usage-notes commit and added adjacent Condition.code guidance for "risk of" and "fear of".
Expanded the Condition.code notes and condition-code value set guidance for "no known problems" without removing the FHIR-7504 history/good-health sentence.
Added the separate Assertions of Condition Absence section, clarifying when questionnaire-style absence/history questions should use QuestionnaireResponse or Observation.
A later no-change decision for latent/history-like concerns supports using Condition.code or text rather than changing clinicalStatus.
